I've reworked the screen at **http://maker:4001** (just refresh the page). Two things changed, and I'd like you to walk through each:

**1. Editing the fetched details.** Paste `https://example.com` again and wait for the details to load. This time the title and description appear in **editable fields** (with a small "✓ filled in for you — edit if you like" hint). Try changing the title text to something of your own. Does having them editable right there, pre-filled but yours to correct, match what you wanted?

**2. Saving when the lookup fails.** Now paste a link that I've set up to *simulate* an unreachable site: `https://timeout.example`. Watch what happens after the lookup attempt.

What you should see: a gentle amber notice — *"Couldn't reach that page for details — you can still save it. Add a title yourself below"* — with the title/description fields empty and ready for you, **and the Save button still active.** Type a title and save it.

Confirm for me: does the failure case behave the way you'd want — never trapping you, letting you save with your own title? And if you save without typing a title at all, I've made it fall back to using the link itself as the title — does that seem sensible, or would you rather be nudged to enter one?
